references.text: Reuben tore his clothes when he discovered that Joseph was missing, an expression of deep grief that mirrors Jephthah's reaction when he saw his daughter.
Jacob tore his clothes in sorrow over the loss of Joseph, the same expression of grief that Jephthah showed.
The law regarding vows to the Lord that cannot be broken, explaining why Jephthah said he could not take back his vow.
The commandment to keep vows made to the Lord, emphasizing the seriousness of Jephthah's situation.
The warning against hasty vows to God, relevant to Jephthah's unconsidered vow.
David tore his clothes as a sign of grief, the same action that Jephthah performed.
Achan brought trouble (עֹכֵר) upon Israel, the same Hebrew root that Jephthah uses for his daughter who has become his trouble.
Jesus' teaching on vows and oaths, which warns against swearing at all, relevant to the consequences of Jephthah's vow.
